title: Raider archetype
description: An armed hostile human, drawn by the director as a band and walked in from the edge of the district. A raider is a survivor-shaped body with `allegiance.faction` set against the colony -- everything that then happens to them (melee, ranged, wounds, bleeding, being chased by zombies) is machinery that already existed, so adding an archetype is a JSON file and no code. Deliberately NOT a survivor entry: the survivor schema forbids unknown keys and its validator enforces aptitudes summing to 15, `SimSurvivors.list_uniques` boots everything under survivors/ whose id starts with survivor.unique., and the frozen TypeScript oracle reads a fixed list of content directories, which this one is not on. NOTE: the Godot content validator is shallow -- it checks top-level types, enums and patterns and rejects unexpected top-level keys, but does not recurse into `aptitudes`, `kit` or `appearance`. check_m2_raiders.gd is the gate that does, and it is why a wrong key inside a nested block cannot sit here unnoticed the way one did in item.wrap.cloth's armor block.

id.description: Stable namespaced id. Permanent once shipped.

allegiance.description: Which side this archetype fights on, copied onto the spawned body's `allegiance` component and read by SimAllegiance.hostile. One value for now on purpose: docs/18's factions are Milestone 3, and an enum with one member is the seam they widen rather than a system pretending to exist.

weight.description: Relative draw weight within a band. Omitted counts as 1.

speed.description: Approach speed in metres per second. Between a shambler's walk and a colonist hurrying to a job: a band on its way somewhere, not a charge.

aptitudes.description: STR/DEX/CON, same three the survivor generator rolls and the same 3..8 clamp SimAptitudes applies. Unlike a survivor entry these are not budget-checked -- a raider is not a colonist and does not draw from the colony's 15 points. A value is either one number, which every body of the archetype shares, or a two-element [min, max] range rolled per body on the `raiderRoll` stream: two scavengers are not the same man, and the jitter is what makes one fight go differently from the next. check_m2_raiders.gd recurses both shapes, because the shallow validator cannot see inside this block.

kit.description: What this archetype arrives carrying. Anything with an equipSlot goes into the hand it belongs to (a weapon in a satchel raises no meleeWeapon and would make the raid a walk); the rest goes in the pack. An entry is a bare item id, or an object when the quantity or the odds matter -- ammunition forced the first, since a pistol arriving with a single round is a raider who fires once and then reloads for the rest of the night, and telling one body of a band from another forced the second. Every id must exist in the item registry and every count must be a positive integer; check_m2_raiders.gd asserts both, because the shallow validator cannot see inside an array.

count.description: Quantity for a stackable base. SimItems clamps it to the base's own stack limit.

chance.description: Odds this row arrives at all, rolled per body on the `raiderRoll` stream; a row that declares none always arrives. This is what makes two scavengers carry different things -- and it belongs on the extras, never on the weapon: a second weapon behind odds is a raider who sometimes also has a knife, but an archetype whose every armed row could roll away would send an unarmed pedestrian at your gate, which is why check_m2_raiders.gd requires each archetype to declare at least one weapon that always arrives.

oneOf.description: [min, max], inclusive, rolled per body. min may equal max.

appearance.description: What this ARCHETYPE looks like, and it is still one body for all of them: which raider is carrying the gun is exactly the sort of certainty the hardcore contract's information clause refuses the player, so a second sprite here would be a free read on the band's loadout. Omit the block entirely and presentation/appearance.gd falls back to the `raider` role colour, which is the normal state until art exists. Since the individuals slice a raider ALSO carries a rolled `raider.person.look`, one id from `content/colony/raider_looks.json` resolved in `content/colony/looks.json`, and the renderer prefers it over this block. That pool is drawn on its own stream with no idea which archetype asked, so a scav and a gunhand can and do wear the same one; every entry in it declares this same sprite and no tint, because `raider_drab` sits at the floor of the palette's ground-contrast guard and a tint can only darken it (check_m2_raiders.gd's LOOKS lane computes the headroom). So a look says nothing about a body today and is the hook per-body art attaches to; what a raider visibly varies by is what they are WEARING, which is kit -- and the worn rows must be identical across archetypes at identical odds, or a cap would answer 'which one has the gun'. NO-TELL is that sentence made mechanical.

sprite.description: Registry key, resolved to assets/sprites/<key>.png. A key, not a path.

tint.description: Colour for the procedural fallback, and a modulate over the sprite when one exists.
